message.content:
I don’t have real‑time access to live air‑quality feeds, so I can’t tell you the exact AQI for Los Angeles at this moment.  

**What you can do instead:**

| Source | How to use it | Typical metrics |
|--------|---------------|-----------------|
| **AirNow.gov** | Enter “Los Angeles” or your ZIP code → see current AQI, pollutant breakdown (PM₂.₅, PM₁₀, O₃, NO₂, CO, SO₂). | AQI scale 0–500; “Good” (0–50), “Moderate” (51–100), “Unhealthy for Sensitive Groups” (101–150), etc. |
| **EPA’s Air Quality Index app** | Download on iOS/Android → real‑time alerts. | Same AQI categories. |
| **Local news sites** (e.g., LA Times, KABC) | Check their “weather” or “environment” sections. | Often provide a quick summary and health advisories. |
| **Weather apps** (Weather.com, AccuWeather) | Look for the “Air Quality” tab. | Usually shows AQI and pollutant levels. |

If you’re planning outdoor activities, it’s a good idea to check one of those sources right before you head out. If you need historical trends or a forecast, most of those sites also offer a 5‑day forecast and past data.
